headline: Warsh comments push Bitcoin above $60,000 as Metaplanet adds $170M to its treasury
summary: Bitcoin crossed $60,000 for the first time in weeks after Federal Reserve Governor Kevin Warsh made remarks that traders read as favorable for risk assets — pulling Solana, Ethereum, and Dogecoin higher alongside it. Metaplanet, a Japanese investment firm, added another $170 million in Bitcoin to bring its total holdings to 43,000 BTC, one of the largest corporate treasuries outside the US. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 19 (Extreme Fear), a reminder that the broader mood remains cautious even as prices tick up.

winners.name: MemeCore
winners.catalyst: MemeCore surged 68.85% with no clear fundamental catalyst — the move appears speculative, consistent with the outsized volatility typical of low-cap memecoin assets.

losers.name: LAB
losers.catalyst: LAB fell 6.85% amid broadly cautious sentiment, with the Fear & Greed Index sitting at 19 (Extreme Fear) weighing on smaller, less liquid assets.

whyItMoved:
The day's main catalyst was a set of public remarks from Kevin Warsh, a former Federal Reserve governor and widely watched commentator on monetary policy. Traders interpreted his comments as supportive of looser financial conditions — the kind of signal that tends to lift risk assets including crypto. Bitcoin responded by crossing $60,000, a level it had been struggling to hold in recent sessions, rising 2.61% on the day.

Solana was the standout among large-caps, gaining 4.24% to $78.34. Zcash also moved sharply, up 4.62% to $419.72, though with no specific news catalyst — the move looks more like a spillover from the broader rally than a Zcash-specific story. Ethereum gained 2.74% to $1,621.92, broadly in line with Bitcoin's move.

Layered on top of the Warsh catalyst was Metaplanet's announcement that it purchased another $170 million in Bitcoin, expanding its treasury to 43,000 BTC. Corporate treasury buying of this scale reinforces a demand narrative that long-term Bitcoin holders appear to share — on-chain data shows that cohort has returned to net accumulation after months of distribution.

Despite the green across the board, the Fear & Greed Index at 19 (Extreme Fear) signals that the market's underlying mood has not shifted. Single-day rallies in fear territory often reflect short-covering or macro-driven pops rather than a sustained change in sentiment. XRP edged up 1.66%, with whale wallet activity picking up even as retail participation stayed muted.
worthKnowing: Solana launched on-chain governance today, requiring 100,000 SOL staked to participate — a structural step toward decentralizing protocol decisions that had previously been made off-chain.
XRP's 1.66% gain came alongside a reported rise in large-wallet (whale) activity, while retail trading volumes remained subdued.
Bitcoin's long-term holders — wallets that have not moved coins in over 155 days — returned to net accumulation this week, according to on-chain data cited by CoinDesk.
